cls: Cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive / liquid embolic agent
pharm: Surgical tissue adhesive and embolic agent (medical device)
quick: Per procedure; injected/applied by specialist (not weight-based)
No systemic drug exposure expected from local use
Used in hepatic varices; procedural judgement
summary: N-Butyl-2-cyanoacrylate is a liquid monomer tissue adhesive and embolic agent (regulated as a medical device, not an FDA-approved drug). On contact with tissue moisture or blood it polymerizes rapidly into a solid, used for skin/wound closure, endoscopic injection of bleeding gastric varices, and embolization of arteriovenous malformations and other vascular lesions (typically mixed with iodized oil/Lipiodol to slow polymerization and add radio-opacity). Dosing is procedure-specific and operator-dependent. Key hazards are premature polymerization, non-target embolization and adhesion to delivery equipment.
indications: Topical skin closure of clean, easily approximated wound edges
Endoscopic injection (cyanoacrylate obturation) of bleeding gastric/oesophageal varices
Embolization of arteriovenous malformations, fistulae and selected hypervascular lesions (interventional radiology)

dosage.d: Thin layer applied over apposed, dry wound edges; 2-3 layers as needed
dosage.n: Do not apply within the wound or to infected tissue

dosage.d: Aliquots (commonly ~0.5-1 mL of glue, often 1:1 with Lipiodol) per injection
dosage.n: Operator-titrated to obliterate varix; flush catheter promptly

dosage.d: Diluted with iodized oil (e.g., 1:1 to 1:4) and injected under fluoroscopy
dosage.n: Concentration sets polymerization speed; avoid catheter entrapment

admin: Use only by trained surgeons/endoscopists/interventional radiologists
For skin: apply to dry, approximated edges; keep adhesive out of the wound and away from eyes
For endovascular/endoscopic use: mix with iodized oil (Lipiodol) to delay polymerization and provide radio-opacity
Avoid contact with metal needles/scopes longer than necessary - it bonds to instruments
Coat or flush the delivery catheter (e.g., with dextrose) to prevent gluing the catheter in place
moa: N-Butyl-2-cyanoacrylate is a liquid monomer that undergoes rapid anionic polymerization on contact with the hydroxyl ions in tissue fluids, blood or moisture, forming a solid adhesive cast. In wounds it bonds approximated edges; in vessels it solidifies within and occludes the lumen, producing mechanical embolization and an inflammatory/fibrotic response that permanently obliterates the target vessel or varix.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cyanoacrylate or formaldehyde
Application to infected, contaminated or actively bleeding/wet wound surfaces (skin use)
Mucosal surfaces or within the wound margin (skin adhesive)
relative: Lesions where non-target embolization would be hazardous
Areas of high tension or across joints (skin)
monitor: Signs of non-target or distal embolization

preg: As a locally applied/implanted device there is minimal systemic drug exposure; use during pregnancy is a procedure-level decision weighing the clinical benefit against any procedural (e.g., radiation for embolization) risk.
lact: No meaningful systemic absorption is expected from local application, so breastfeeding is not affected by the adhesive itself.
renal: No systemic dose adjustment; the agent acts locally. For embolization procedures, account for contrast-related renal risk separately.
hepatic: Used endoscopically for gastric varices in patients with liver disease; there is no systemic dose adjustment, but procedural risk in advanced liver disease must be considered.

major: None pharmacologic - hazards are procedural (e.g., embolic migration)
moderate: Iodized oil (Lipiodol) - intentionally co-administered to modulate polymerization rate and add radio-opacity
minor: Moisture/blood at the site - accelerates polymerization
interactions.diagnostics: The polymerized cast (especially mixed with Lipiodol) is radio-opaque and visible on imaging; it can create artifact on CT/MRI.

common: Local inflammation or transient pain at application/injection site
serious: Non-target / distal embolization (including pulmonary or systemic)
Ulceration, rebleeding or perforation after variceal injection

monitoring: Fluoroscopic/endoscopic confirmation of correct placement and absence of distal embolization
Post-procedure observation for embolic complications and rebleeding
Signs of infection or local tissue reaction
counsel: This is a medical adhesive applied during your procedure, not a medicine you take
For skin closure: keep the area dry, do not pick at the film, and let it slough off naturally
Report increasing pain, redness, swelling, discharge or wound separation
After embolization/variceal treatment, report sudden chest pain, breathlessness or bleeding (e.g., vomiting blood, black stools)
pk: Polymerizes within seconds of contact with tissue moisture/blood
Solid cast forms almost immediately on application
Not applicable - acts locally; not systemically absorbed in significant amounts
Permanent (skin film sloughs over 5-10 days; vascular cast persists)
Store cool and dry in sealed ampoule/applicator; protect from moisture; single use
pearls: Regulated as a medical device (not an FDA-approved systemic drug) - information is based on device labeling and procedural literature
Mixing with iodized oil (Lipiodol) slows polymerization and adds radio-opacity for controlled embolization
Major hazards are non-target embolization and gluing the catheter/instrument in place
For skin: apply only over the surface of dry, approximated edges - never within the wound
Polymerizes on contact with any moisture, so keep the field and delivery system appropriately prepared
missed: Not applicable - this is a single-use adhesive/embolic agent applied during a procedure, not a scheduled medication.
overdose: There is no systemic 'overdose'; the relevant risk is using too large a volume or too rapid injection, causing non-target or distal (e.g., pulmonary) embolization and excessive tissue reaction. Management is procedural and supportive, directed at any embolic complication.
